_comment: The figures of the approved board, as data. This file is what the golden
test renders, so the frozen artefact is the board that was signed off
rather than a fresh invention of it.
Counts and labels only. No colours, no widths, no percentages, no markup:
everything presentational is derived in pipeline/report/
leadership_render.py. Write text with literal characters (& — < >); the
renderer escapes it. Numbers in the read-out carry the ’ separator the
rest of CPLAN prints, because validate() compares them against the
board's own figures spelled the same way.
WHERE THESE FIGURES COME FROM. The portfolio counts and the per-value
`activities` figures are the pack's own: 01-summary.txt · VOLUME and
06-breakdowns.csv · measure=activities, from the 2026-08-12 generation.
The `leadership` figures are NOT. In that pack every with_executives
measure is 0, because the seed generator never fills the source system's
bod_geb field, so a board rendered from it would carry five empty panels
and could not be judged. The leadership counts below are demo figures,
consistent with the structure the pack guarantees -- the exclusive bands
close on 312, the overlapping blocks deliberately sum past it -- and they
are what to replace first when a pack with the field filled in arrives.
The bands are listed in band order and stay in it. The divisions and
regions may be listed in any order; the renderer ranks them.
title: Leadership attention
subtitle: Where executive time is going, and where it is missing.
readout: Leadership involvement is recorded on 312 of the 2’400 activities in scope, or 13% of the plan. Group Functions binds the most executive attention at 118 activities, well ahead of Global Wealth Management at 96, while Technology records 27 against a division volume of 384. Involvement rises with planned audience size — 111 of the 312 sit in the largest band, against 21 in the smallest — and 995 activities in scope fall in the top two bands, so the plan holds large-audience communication that records no leadership at all. Consider reviewing where that gap is deliberate.
